_comment: How a slideshow post is dressed: the caption line, the hashtags, the type on
the slides, and which destinations the pipeline leans toward.
Everything here is editorial rather than structural, it is the set of
decisions that get re-litigated after looking at a week of numbers, so it
lives in one file you can edit without reading any code. src/postConfig.js
reads it, validates it, and is the only module that knows this path.
Read once per process and cached, exactly as sources.json and
destinations.json are. A malformed file throws at first use rather than
quietly reverting to a default: a post that silently lost its hashtags looks
identical to a post that never had any.
_angles_comment: THE ISRAELI ANGLE. MOVED UP A LEVEL, AND IT NOW STEERS DECKS TOO.
The things that make a post about Rome a post for THIS audience.
BRIEF.md rule 2 is 'be specific', and the half of it that is easy to
forget is the Israeli half: a post that would read identically to an
American audience has nothing in it for this one. This list is the only
thing the account has that a hundred repost archives posting the same
photographs do not.
It used to live under `shoot` and reach exactly one kind of post: the
shoot, which is the one thing here the bot cannot make. One a day, on the
format that waits for somebody to pick up a camera, while every format
that actually runs unattended chose its subject with no angle at all.
`shoot.angles` is still read and folded in, so nothing breaks.
WHAT AN ANGLE MAY DO ONCE A PIPELINE HAS ONE, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT.
On a shoot the angle is the CONTENT: you are the source, you know whether
the flight is direct, and the shot list says so.
Nothing automated knows any of that. A deck that printed
'טיסה ישירה מנתב״ג' on a slide would be inventing a fact of exactly the
kind the rest of this project refuses to invent, and inventing it on the
claims an Israeli traveller is most likely to ACT on. So for anything the
bot publishes by itself the angle steers SELECTION and stops there: it
decides which destination is worth a deck this week, not what the deck
says about it. 'חופשת סוכות' makes an October-good destination the one
that gets proposed; it does not put the word Sukkot on a slide.
src/angles.js carries that warning into every prompt that receives one,
because it is the instruction a model will quietly disobey by being
helpful.

_comment: One of these opens every published slideshow, picked at random per post.
THE CTA CAME BACK, AND THE URL DID NOT. See BRIEF.md.
The old caption was `למתכנן טיולים חכם בביו שלנו` over `www.tiyulplus.com`
and it was removed on the argument that an external domain in a TikTok
description is a demotion and was never tappable anyway. That argument was
about the DOMAIN and it still holds: format.js refuses to hand a caption
carrying one to the approval queue, so a line added here with a domain in
it fails loudly at build time rather than being published.
What is restored is the pointer with no domain in it, `הלינק בביו`, at
the END of the caption, on `ctaShare` of posts rather than on all of them.
The brief's rule is 'a soft one at the end', and a CTA on every single
post is not soft; it is the whole caption wearing a different hat.
`questions` is the other half of the brief's caption shape: one short line
plus a question. The question is what a comment is an answer TO, a
caption that states and stops gives nobody anything to type.
_ctas_comment: THE CLOSING ASK. A POOL NOW, AND THE URL IS GONE FROM EVERY ENTRY.
This was one string, `cta`, pointing at the bio. The singular key is
still read and folded into the pool, so nothing breaks, but one string
is a signature however soft the wording is - the same argument that
turned the fixed caption into `lines` twenty entries ago.
WHAT THE ASKS NOW ASK FOR, AND WHY IN THIS ORDER.
A send is the most valuable thing a caption can buy. Instagram's own
ranking weights sends per reach several times higher than likes when
deciding whether to show a post to somebody who does not follow you,
and this account has no followers to speak of, so non-follower reach is
the only reach there is. `שלחו את זה למי שאתם טסים איתו` asks for
exactly that signal, in the one situation where a viewer genuinely has
somebody to send it to: nobody plans a trip alone.
A follow is the second. It is what turns one post's reach into the next
post's baseline, and the brief's rule 7 is that reach without follows is
the seven-video problem in a better costume.
A save is third. It is a real ranking signal and it is the honest ask on
a post somebody is not going to act on today.
The bio pointer survives as ONE entry out of several rather than as the
whole of it. It is not a URL - `assertNoUrl` and postConfig both still
refuse those - and the bio is the only tappable route to the product
either platform offers, so a pipeline that never mentions it is a
pipeline that never sends anybody anywhere. One post in several is the
share that keeps it from reading as an advertisement.

_questions_comment: A QUESTION WHOSE ANSWER IS INFORMATION THE READER HAS.
The previous pool asked things like `לאן אתם טסים הבא?` and
`מי כבר היה שם?`. Both are answerable, and that is the problem: they are
answerable in one word, by anybody, without knowing anything. A one-word
comment is worth almost nothing as a signal and worth nothing at all to
the next reader, so the thread under the post stays empty even when
somebody does reply.
Two shapes replace them, and both ask for something only a particular
reader can give:
- A PRICE OR A DETAIL from somebody who has been. `כמה יצא לכם ליום`
is a question with a number in the answer, and the numbers people
post in the comments are the most useful thing on the post.
- A BINARY CHOICE. `זה או יעד חוף?` gets answered more than an open
question does, because picking one of two costs nothing and having an
opinion is the whole appeal.
The Israeli angle is in here too, on purpose, for the reason the brief's
rule 2 gives: a question that would read identically to an American
audience is a question with nothing in it for this one. A direct flight
from Ben Gurion and what a trip cost in shekels are things this audience
asks each other and nobody else.

זה או יעד חוף? תחליטו לי
כמה הייתם מוכנים לשלם על זה?
שלושה ימים מספיקים או מעט מדי?
_lines_comment: THE OPENING LINE. REWRITTEN FROM MOODS TO REASONS.
The pool was twenty moods: `נראה כמו ציור`, `הנוף עוצר נשימה`,
`פשוט קסם`, `הלב נשאר שם`. Every one of them is a reaction to the
picture, which means every one of them is a line the viewer has already
had by the time they read it. The picture said `beautiful` faster and
better than the caption can, so the caption's first line was spent
agreeing with it.
That matters more than it reads, because of what the first line is FOR.
It is the only part of the caption most people see, it is what decides
whether the rest gets read, and on Instagram the thing worth buying with
it is a SEND: nobody forwards a friend a pretty picture of a place
neither of them can name, and a send is weighted far above a like when
the platform decides whether to show a post to somebody who does not
follow you.
So a line here now does one of three things, and none of them is
admiring the photograph:
- NAMES WHO IT IS FOR. `למי שיש 4 ימים ולא יודע לאן` is a line a
reader either is or is not, and the ones who are have somebody to
send it to.
- SAYS WHAT IT IS WORTH KEEPING FOR. `תשמרו את זה לפעם הבאה שתתכננו`
is an instruction with a reason in it.
- SAYS SOMETHING ONLY THIS AUDIENCE WOULD SAY. Distance in flight
hours from here, what fits in a long weekend, where the school
holiday crowd is not. BRIEF.md rule 2's Israeli half.
None of them claims a fact. `ארבע שעות טיסה` is not on this list and
will not be: the pipeline does not know that, and the angle rules
(`_angles_comment`) apply to a caption exactly as they apply to a slide.
What is here is framing, which is ours to write, rather than facts,
which are not.

_comment: Exactly `broadCount + nicheCount` tags under every post, five, by default.
Broad tags buy the first impressions and niche tags decide who the post is
then shown to, so the split matters more than the total. Two and three is
the mix this account is testing.
`useDestination` spends ONE of the niche slots on a tag generated from the
deck's own country, #פורטוגל on a Portugal deck, rather than adding a
sixth tag. The count stays exactly five either way; when the deck's country
cannot be resolved the slot falls back to the niche pool.
#fyp AND #foryou WERE REMOVED, AND THEN SO WERE #פוריו AND #ויראלי.
The first removal was right and did not go far enough. Its argument was
that a broad tag should buy the first impressions from a POOL this post
could plausibly win in, and that #fyp is every video on the application,
which is not a pool, it is the whole app. #פוריו was then chosen as the
same request made in the language the audience types in - which is to
say, the same non-pool with Hebrew letters. #ויראלי is worse: it
describes a hoped-for outcome rather than a subject, so there is no
audience on the other side of it to be shown to.
Both are gone. The broad pool is now broad WITHIN TRAVEL and nothing
else: #טיול, #חופשה, #טיסות, #תיירות, #עולם.
AND THIS IS THE LAST TIME THIS BLOCK IS WORTH TUNING.
Instagram's own head has said plainly that hashtags do not improve
reach, and the cap is five. They still do real work on TikTok, where
they are one of the signals that decides which topic a video is filed
under, which is why five topical ones stay rather than none.
But the effort that has gone into the broad/niche split here is out of
all proportion to what the split can buy, and it is effort that was not
going into watch time, into the opening line, or into whether the post
is worth sending to somebody. If this file gets another hour, it should
not be this block that gets it.
The type on a TikTok slide. Small, light, off to one side, a caption
somebody typed on their own photograph, not a graphic laid over stock.
`sizePct` is measured against `sizeBasis`, and the basis is the frame's
WIDTH. That makes 0.045 a 49px name on a 1080x1920 frame.
The number was arrived at twice. The brief said '~3% of canvas height
(roughly 30px)', and those two do not agree: 3% of 1920 is 58px and 3% of
1080 is 32px. 32 was built first, on the reading that 'roughly 30px' was
the firmer half of the sentence, and it shipped slides whose names could
not be read on a busy street photograph. 49px is where it landed after
looking at four renders of the same hard frame side by side, and it is
also, independently, about what the reference accounts use: lucyysarchive
sets a place name at roughly 2.5% of frame height, which is 48px here.
Two lessons are baked into that, and both are why `adapt` below exists:
type size is not a legibility mechanism on its own, and a percentage with
no stated basis is not a specification.
`bands` are the vertical thirds the text is allowed into, as fractions of
the frame, and `x` pins it to the left. The placement search still runs,
it decides which of the two bands the photograph can actually carry, and
what colour the type has to be, but it can no longer land in the middle.
`assist` is the soft elliptical wash that fades in only when the measured
contrast was not enough on its own. It is not a background box and cannot
become one; turn it off and a slide over a busy frame ships illegible.
The values above are a FLOOR, not a constant, and this is the block
that makes them one.
Small, light, 90% and one soft shadow is the right treatment for a name
sitting on quiet sky. Applied unconditionally it is also how a slide
ships illegible: the previous version of this file set exactly those
four numbers as fixed values, and a place name landing where a dark
planter met bright paving, about 2:1 contrast, had nothing left to
defend it. Four reductions at once, and the one mechanism that used to
adapt had been turned into a constant at the same time.
So each is now a floor that rises with the shortfall render/photo.js
measured for THIS photograph. On a clean frame nothing here fires and
the slide looks exactly as specified. On a hard one the type thickens,
goes fully opaque and gets a real shadow under it, which is what the
reference accounts do too; their type is light because their frames are
chosen, not because light type always works.
Set all three to 0 / equal-to-base to get the old fixed behaviour back.
Short vertical videos: a stock clip with one line of Hebrew burned onto it.
A different format from a deck, and the difference is what the text DOES.
A slide labels the picture, 'סקוגאפוס, איסלנד'. A clip's line does not
describe the footage at all: it names a mundane Israeli moment and lets the
video be the daydream that answers it. 'על מה אני חושב בשיעור מתמטיקה' over
a forest trail is the whole format.
That is also why this format does not fight verify.js. A line that makes no
claim about WHERE the footage was shot has nothing to source, so a generic
trail can carry it honestly, where 'מפלים באיסלנד' over the same clip
would be a place claim with a stock uploader's title as its only evidence.
Lines are written per clip by src/video/hooks.js by FILLING A KNOWN FORMAT,
not by free composition. That distinction took four rejected rounds to find.
Every reference post the owner supplied is a recognizable meme template:
"has to be top 5 X oat" (284K), "one of the coolest feelings..." (229K, also
a ranking), "Average X in Y" (130K), "Fuck X go to Y" (1.5K). None is an
original sentence. The virality lives in the FORMAT - the viewer recognizes
it instantly, and the joke is applying it to this footage.
Free composition produces the opposite type: clever observations with
metaphors and personification, which read as copywriting however casual the
wording is. The formats below are the menu; edit them, add new ones lifted
from real posts, delete ones that stop working. This list IS the voice of
the account.
THIS LIST CAME BACK, and what replaced it is worth knowing about.
For a while the formats here were the brief's advice shapes - "3 טעויות
שישראלים עושים בגאורגיה", "5 ימים ברומא ב-2,000 ₪ - ככה" - and each hook
came with two to five BEATS under it: the lines that deliver what the hook
promised, burned in one after another over a twenty-six second clip.
The writing did what it was asked. The VIDEO did not. Underneath those
four changing lines is one stock shot that never cuts, so the footage stops
being the post and becomes wallpaper for a caption rewriting itself - a
slideshow with a video background, which is a different and worse format
than the one this account is.
The advice shapes are not deleted for being bad. They belong to a post type
where every line change is a CUT, with new footage under each beat, and
that type does not exist yet. Until it does a clip is one line held for its
whole length, which is what these formats are built for.
git show 97ec1c1 has the whole of it: the advice formats, their beat
examples, the prompt, the per-beat guards and the timeline that spaced
them. Lift it from there rather than writing it again.

_comment: DESTINATION-FIRST. This is the correction for the fault that produced four
bike videos on anonymous roads.
The queries used to ask for a camera technique - "pov walking mountain",
"hiking pov" - and a stock library answers that literally: handlebars on an
empty road, which matches every word and is nowhere. Measured with a vision
judge, every clip those queries returned scored 0-4 out of 10 on "would a
viewer want to travel here". Across 235 clips from POV queries, exactly 7
were both a real destination and a participant camera.
Searching the destinations instead returns Gullfoss, the Dolomites, Oia,
Vernazza, Lauterbrunnen - ~85% scoring 7+ - and a good share of those are
POV anyway. So POV is now a PREFERENCE applied inside destination-worthy
results rather than the axis everything is selected on.
The list leads with the countries in destinations.weights above, because
that is where this audience actually flies. Editing it is editing what the
account is about.
_spectator_comment: A person named in the title is a person in the FRAME, which means somebody is
standing back filming them, and that is a stock lifestyle shot however good
This list is the correction for the filter's first version, which had only
prefer and reject and therefore ranked by SUBJECT. It scored "woman walking in
autumn forest pathway" at 5 and "scenic hike behind a majestic waterfall" at 2:
the first hits four forest words while being a shot of a model, the second hits
two while being exactly the format. Every clip the owner rejected by name
Matched as WHOLE WORDS, which is load-bearing. "hiker" is a person being
filmed and "hiking" is the activity, and the prefix matching used for prefer
cannot tell them apart, that exact pair is what got through.
A penalty rather than a veto, so an explicit POV marker can outrun it: "pov
hiker on a ridge" is a participant and should survive.
_vision_comment: The judge runs on the Pexels thumbnail, which the API already returns - no
download, one cheap call per candidate.
visionMinDestination is the whole filter. 7 keeps Santorini, the Dolomites
and Gullfoss; it rejects an empty road, which scores 0-3. The owner rejected
two clips by eye and the judge had independently scored them 0 and 3.
rejectPersonSubject is the owner's rule, and it is a veto rather than a
price. A clip went out of somebody standing in front of the view, and
rejectStaged did not stop it: staged asks whether the shot is a MODEL
SHOOT, and a man simply standing at a viewpoint is not posed and is not
selling anything, so the judge answered no. What is wrong with it is not
that it is fake - it is that the camera is a SPECTATOR and the post is
then about a stranger rather than about the place. An aerial is the right
subject from the wrong height and is worth keeping at a price; a person
filmed in front of the place is the wrong subject, and no destination
score makes it the right one.
The judge is told what does NOT count: a hand on a railing, a boot on a
step, two walkers the size of a thumbnail on a ridge. That carve-out is
load-bearing - POV footage always has a body edge in it, and preferPov
says this account wants POV.
rejectAerialOnly is still false, and aerialPenalty is why. A drone shot went
out on a /clip batch and should not have: BRIEF.md lists 'another stock
landscape' under Never, and an aerial is the purest form of it. But a drone
of Lauterbrunnen is still somewhere worth going, and vetoing the vantage
outright throws away most of the best destinations on the days nothing else
clears the gate - so it is priced out rather than banned.
4 is arithmetic, not taste. The gate is destination >= 7 and the scale ends
at 10, so the best imaginable drone shot ranks 6 and loses to the weakest
ground clip that got through at 7. An aerial is therefore built only when
the ground returned nothing at all, which is the one case where it is still
better than no clip. It used to cost 1, which a destination score of 9
shrugged off - that is how the batch happened.

_comment: The encode. 1080x1920 H.264, which is what TikTok wants and what every phone
plays without thinking about it.
CRF 23 rather than 21: from a 4K source 21 produced 40MB for 8 seconds,
which is over Telegram's upload limit and far more than 1080 needs. 23 is
about half that and the difference is not visible at this size.
`seconds` IS 8 AGAIN, and this number has been both things now, so the
argument on each side is worth keeping.
It went to 15-35 for the brief (BRIEF.md, rule 6), on sound reasoning: a
longer video carrying the SAME single line is strictly worse - more
seconds for the same information is how average watch time falls under
40%. So the length rose and the content rose with it, a hook plus two to
five beats, computed as hookSeconds + beats × secondsPerBeat.
What that shipped was twenty-six seconds of ONE unchanging stock shot with
the text swapping above it. The brief's length is for a video that keeps
moving; held on a single frozen composition it is half a minute of
wallpaper, and the line stops being the thing the footage answers.
So a clip is one line over eight seconds again, and eight is the length a
single line can carry: there is nothing to stay for after it is read, so
the best outcome is a second lap rather than a slow one. The brief's
15-35 comes back with the post type that earns it - new footage under
every line, which is a cut rather than a caption change.
`loopSource` outlived the beats and is worth keeping. Pexels serves clips
from five seconds up and search.minDuration lets them in; -stream_loop
repeats the input until -t is satisfied, so a five-second source still
fills eight. On scenery with no cut in it the seam is invisible. Turn it
off and a short source is simply trimmed to whatever it has.
`startAt` is a FALLBACK only - overlay.js picks the best window by
measuring frames, and uses this when measurement is unavailable.
THE MUSIC BED, MIXED IN AT RENDER TIME. OFF, AND HERE IS WHY.
`on` is false. The owner picks the sound in each app by hand, which is
the one part of a post this pipeline was never going to do better, and
with the Instagram copy now posted by hand too (see targets.js) there
is no longer a path by which a silent file reaches a feed unattended.
A bed would actively get in the way of that workflow rather than
merely being redundant: adding a sound in the Instagram app to a video
that already has audio MIXES the two, so every post would need the
original muted by hand before the chosen track sounded right.
IT IS KEPT, WORKING AND TESTED, BECAUSE OF WHAT WOULD BRING IT BACK.
It was built for a real problem. Instagram's Content Publishing API
has no draft state and a reel's audio cannot be changed after posting,
so the moment anything publishes a reel unattended, whatever audio the
file carries is permanent. If the Instagram half is ever automated -
because posting by hand every day turns out to be the thing that does
not happen, which is the honest risk - this is what stops it going out
silent, and it is one flag rather than a rebuild.
Which tracks exist, and whether we are allowed to use them, is
assets/audio/tracks.json - a declared list, not a directory listing.
See the long note in that file.
`keepAudio` above and this are mutually exclusive, and a track wins.
`keepAudio` keeps the STOCK clip's own audio, which is almost always a
library music bed somebody else chose; on a cuts clip it would be four
different beds changing at every cut. When a track is mixed in, the
source audio is dropped whatever keepAudio says.
`volume` is well under 1 on purpose. This is a bed under a burned-in
line, not the point of the post, and a bed at full level is the single
most common way a travel clip announces that it was assembled.
`fadeOutSeconds` matters more than it looks on an eight-second clip:
the whole value of that length is that it loops, and a bed cut off
mid-bar at the loop point is a click on every lap.
`maxOffsetSeconds` is how far into the track a clip may start, chosen
from the clip's own id so a re-render sounds the same. Without it every
post opens on the same few bars, which with a handful of tracks is the
most automated-sounding thing a feed can do. Set 0 to always start at
the beginning.
THE SECOND CLIP SHAPE: SEVERAL SHOTS, CUT, A LINE PER CUT.
A clip has two shapes now and neither replaces the other.
held  one stock shot, one line, eight seconds. Unchanged.
cuts  four or five shots, four seconds each, a line on every one.
This is the post type BRIEF.md and video/hooks.js both promised and
parked. The beats were written, guarded and then reverted, and the
reason was never the writing: under four changing lines sat one stock
shot that never cut, so the footage became wallpaper for a caption
rewriting itself. The note in clips.video says the brief's 15-35
seconds 'comes back with the post type that earns it - new footage
under every line, which is a cut rather than a caption change'. This
is that type.
WHAT THE LINES SAY, AND WHY THIS IS NOT THE OLD ADVICE FORMAT.
The parked formats were advice - `3 טעויות שישראלים עושים בגאורגיה`,
`5 ימים ברומא ב-2,000 ₪` - and every beat under them was a fact no
page published: a price nobody quoted, a mistake nobody reported. That
is a real cost and BRIEF.md already counted it once for the fare ban.
Paying it four more times per video, unattended, on a format that runs
on a timer, is not the same bargain.
So a cut's beats are LABELS, not claims: the place in the shot, which
is the one thing about a stock clip this pipeline actually establishes
- the vision judge names it, the pin under every clip already prints
it, and the country hashtag is generated from it. A beat is the same
fact the deck slide carries (`סקוגאפוס, איסלנד`), and it is sourced by
exactly the mechanism that sources those.
Which makes the hook a COUNT and a theme over places the pipeline can
name, and `beatCountMismatch` in video/cuts.js is what holds the two
together: a hook promising five places over four cuts is the broken
promise that cost the beats their first outing, and it is the one rule
here that cannot be waived.
LENGTH. Four seconds a cut, four or five cuts, so 16 to 20 seconds -
inside the brief's 15 to 35, and arrived at from the other end: four
seconds is long enough to read a place name and see the shot move, and
short enough that nothing is held after it has been understood.
_hook_comment: The opening line names how many places are coming and what they have
in common. It is the only line in a cut that is written rather than
read off the footage, so it is also the only one that can be wrong.
`maxWords` is looser than a held clip's, because this line carries a
number and a theme where a held clip's carries a thought.

hookFormats.desc: "<מספר> מקומות ש<תכונה>". התכונה היא משהו שרואים בפריים - לא נראים אמיתיים, נראים מצוירים, אין בהם אף אחד. בלי טענה על מחיר, עונה או מסמכים.
"<מספר> יעדים ש<תכונה>" או "<מספר> מקומות ב<מדינה>". השם של המדינה מותר רק אם כל הקטעים באותה מדינה, וזה נאמר לך.
"<מספר> מקומות ששווה לשמור" או "<מספר> יעדים לרשימה". הזמנה לשמור, בלי להבטיח מידע שאין בסרטון.

_comment: Read off five real posts and then tuned against rendered batches by the owner.
Centred-ish, upper area, bold, NO STROKE. The stroke was added because it is
what TikTok's own text tool produces and what the Hebrew reference posts use,
and it was then removed on sight: at this size over these frames it reads as
an outline rather than as native text. Legibility now rests on the adaptive
shadow and the wash, both of which respond to what render/photo.js measured.
One colour, #FFF4B3, chosen by the owner. The palette used to hold white too
and a third of posts drew it, white was rejected on sight twice.
Position is NOT fixed: xs offers three columns and the measurement picks the
one whose sky is actually empty. Pinning it to the centre put text on a cliff
while clear sky sat unused either side.
_width_comment: Narrow ON PURPOSE, and this is the number that decides whether a line looks
At 0.72 the block is 777px on a 1080px frame, and on a picture whose subject
stands in the middle, a tower, a cliff, a waterfall, NO position fits it on
clean sky. The placement search then picks the least-bad straddle and the line
runs from sky onto rock, which is the single most amateur-looking thing these
At 0.46 the same nine-word line wraps to two rows and the whole block fits in
a corner of the sky. Two short rows on clean background beat one long row

_comment: English country name from the vision judge -> how Israelis write it.
A separate list from deck/flags.js on purpose: that one is keyed on ISO
codes off Wikidata, and this one is keyed on free text a model produced.
A country missing here simply means the place formats are not offered for
that clip, which is the safe direction.
The site name from the vision judge -> how THIS account spells it.
The description is Hebrew all the way through, including the names that
are awkward to write, so the judge is asked for a Hebrew spelling
alongside every site it identifies. That works, but a transliteration is
a judgement call and the model does not make the same one every time,
and the same valley spelled two ways across two posts reads worse than
either spelling does on its own.
So the places this feed keeps returning to are pinned here by hand and
this list wins. It never has to be complete: a site that is missing
simply uses the judge's spelling, and a site with no Hebrew at all
leaves the pin naming the country alone.
A SHOOT IS A SHOT LIST, NOT A POST. Nothing here is ever published by the
bot, because the video does not exist until somebody films it.
This is the honest half of BRIEF.md. Rules 3 and 4, show the product, use
real footage, need a camera, a voice and a screen, and no pipeline has
any of those. What a pipeline can do is everything around them: choose the
destination and the angle, rotate the shape so two of a kind never land
back to back, write the hook and the beats and the caption and the tags,
remember which part of which series is next, and refuse to ask during
Shabbat. So it does that, and sends the result to Telegram as a list of
things to film.
The comparison that settled this: @brickdealil, the sister account, holds
500-970 views a video on hand-held product footage with none of this
project's measured typography behind it, while @tiyulplus decayed 672 → 33
on stock. The variable is not production value. It is whether something
real is happening in the frame, and that cannot be automated, only
scheduled, briefed, and made easy enough to actually do.
shoot.cta: תכננו טיול כזה בחינם, הלינק בביו
_productShare_comment: Rule 3 says the product appears in at least half the videos. A weighted
rotation alone does not guarantee that, weights are a tendency and a run
of five non-product shoots is well within normal for any weighting.
So this is enforced rather than weighted: src/shoot/rotation.js counts the
last `productWindow` shoots and, if fewer than `productShare` of them
showed the product, the next one is format C regardless of what the
rotation wanted. The brief's word is 'at least', which is a floor, and a
floor is a check, not a preference.
_series_comment: A series is the cheapest one there is, 'חלק 1 מתוך 3' tells a viewer that
something specific is coming and that the way to get it is to follow. The
bot holds the state, because the whole point is that part 2 arrives and a
series that stops at part 1 is worse than no series at all.
`every` is how often a shoot opens a new series. Not every post: a feed
where everything is part of something is a feed with no standalone entry
point, and a viewer arriving on part 2 of 3 has been handed a middle.
_formats_comment: The brief's five shapes, rule 5. `needsProduct` marks the one that IS the
product demo; `shots` is what the shot list asks you to film, and it is
the field that makes the difference between a brief and a task.

_comment: THE FOURTH PUBLISHED KIND: an itinerary an AI wrote, shown as a slideshow.
"ביקשתי מ-AI לתכנן לי 4 ימים ברומא, הנה מה שיצא", and then the plan
itself, one slide per day, drawn as the product rather than as another
photograph with a caption on it. It is the only post this account makes
where the thing being shown IS the thing being sold, which is rule 3 of the
brief and the rule no other pipeline here can obey.
WHAT IS TRUE ABOUT IT, EXACTLY.
The itinerary is written by Claude, not fetched from the product. The post
says an AI planned it, an AI did plan it, and that is the whole of the
claim. What the post must never do is show a screenshot of the app and
imply the app produced this particular plan - so the slides are drawn in
the account's own design language, plainly ours, and no slide imitates a
screen the product actually has. Wire the real product in and this comment
is what has to change first.
The costs are the same bargain the fare ban made (BRIEF.md): a number here
is nobody's published figure, it is a plan's estimate, and every one of
them is printed on the approval card before you tap. The total is SUMMED
from the stops rather than written by the model - a plan whose own
arithmetic disagrees with itself on screen is the broken-promise failure
that cost the clip format its beats.
`giveaway` is the follow ask, and it is the reason this kind exists at all
rather than being a nicer deck. A plan is worth saving and worth asking a
question under; the month of premium is what turns a save into a comment
and a comment into a follow. The bot writes the ask and prints who it
promised what - it cannot read comments and does not pick winners. That
part is yours, and it is a real promise to real people: switch `on` to
false the day you stop wanting to keep it.
_stops_comment: Three stops is a day somebody could actually do; five is a screenshot of a
spreadsheet. The ceiling is also a layout constraint - at four stops the
day slide is still readable at thumbnail size on a 1080x1920 frame, and
the first thing a viewer does with an itinerary is judge whether it looks
plans.totalNoteHe: כניסות ואטרקציות בלבד, בלי טיסה ולינה
_totalNote_comment: THIS LINE IS NOT DECORATION. The total on the slide is the sum of the stop
prices and nothing else, so a viewer reading "2,340 ₪ ל-4 ימים ברומא"
would otherwise be reading it as the price of the trip, which it is not,
by an order of magnitude once a flight and four nights are in it.
A number that invites the wrong reading is the same defect as a wrong
number. Empty this string and the slide stops saying what its own total

giveaway.captionHe: עקבו ותגיבו "{keyword}", ו-{winners} מכם מקבלים {premiumDays} יום פרימיום עלינו
_comment: The keyword is the destination on purpose. A comment that says "רומא"
is a comment the next viewer reads as a vote for the place rather than
as a raffle entry, and it costs the commenter nothing to mean it.
When an Israeli audience is on the application, and when it is not.
`windows` are local Israel hours, as [from, to). The two are the lunch
break and the evening, which is where this audience is; a post outside
them spends its first-hour test, the one that decides whether there is a
second hour, on a smaller pool than it deserved.
`shabbat` is not a preference. Friday evening to Saturday evening is the
one window where most of this audience is definitively not scrolling, and
a video that lands in it has its whole ranking test run against nobody.
The hours are approximate on purpose: real candle-lighting time moves week
to week with the latitude and the season, and being an hour early on the
Friday and an hour late on the Saturday costs nothing, while computing it
properly would mean shipping a zmanim table to save an hour of reach.
This governs the SHOOT queue, when a shot list is worth sending, because
a shot list is a thing you act on within the hour. It deliberately does
not govern the card and deck drip, which is spaced by POST_INTERVAL and
has its own quiet hours.
Where this account's audience actually flies, weighted.
destinations.json is 102 places chosen for the same reason, but it is a
flat list: the idea generator saw Reykjavik and Athens as equally likely
and the climate rotation reached them in calendar order. Weighting is what
turns 'we cover these' into 'we lead with these'.
Keyed on the Hebrew country name exactly as destinations.json spells it.
A country not listed here gets `defaultWeight`, so this file never has to
be complete, adding a country raises it, removing one does not ban it.
Long-haul and cold destinations are deliberately left at the default
rather than zeroed: they are worth a post occasionally, just not a post
ahead of Greece.
